story_type: moon rocket launch, close-up slow motion
hook: 7.5 million pounds of thrust, filmed right next to the fire.
narration: Seven and a half million pounds of thrust, filmed right next to the fire.
This is a Saturn V, the Moon rocket, three hundred sixty-three feet tall.
Five F-1 engines at its base roared to life together.
As they lit, sheets of ice shook loose and rained down past the cameras.
The tanks held liquid oxygen near three hundred degrees below zero, cold enough to freeze the humid air onto the rocket's skin.
[short pause] Then the giant began to rise past the tower.
outcome: The Saturn V cleared the tower and climbed away on a column of fire.
title: Saturn V liftoff from inside the fire
description:
Slow-motion film from cameras around the launch tower shows a Saturn V Moon rocket igniting its five F-1 engines, shedding ice and lifting off from Kennedy Space Center.

Footage: NASA Marshall Space Flight Center video, via the NASA Image and Video Library: https://images.nasa.gov/details/Ultimate%20Saturn%20V%20Launch%20w%20Enhanced%20Sound
